purpose: A measurement contract for improving usefulness, trust, discoverability, experience and financial viability without inventing baselines or treating vanity metrics as outcomes.

northStars.definition: A sampled visitor finds the intended tool, gets a correct result and can explain the important limitation without assistance.
A listener identifies the artist or track they want and intentionally reaches the verified destination using the visible player or link.

statusPolicy: not-measured is a valid result, never a zero and never permission to invent a number
A target is added only after a dated baseline and an owner-approved decision rule exist
A lab score is not field evidence; Search Console, CrUX, browser tests, bookkeeping and moderated sessions keep their own instruments
A metric cannot override safety, correctness, privacy, accessibility or product-boundary guardrails

metrics.name: Top-task success rate
metrics.unit: percent of moderated sessions
metrics.source: Dated moderated usability sessions using representative tasks; no user input is retained.
metrics.cadence: Per material UX change and quarterly
metrics.decision: Fix the most common blocker before adding catalogue breadth; quantitative claims need a sufficiently sized sample.

metrics.name: Find-to-result time
metrics.unit: seconds, task-level median and spread
metrics.source: Timed moderated task sessions; Search Console query-to-page selection is supporting evidence only.
metrics.decision: Prefer the change that reduces time without reducing correctness or comprehension.

metrics.name: Recoverable failure rate
metrics.unit: percent of sampled failures with a successful recovery
metrics.source: Browser test matrix plus moderated sessions covering empty, invalid, offline and retry states.
metrics.decision: A failure must explain what happened and provide a safe next action; silent failure blocks release.

metrics.name: Result comprehension
metrics.unit: qualitative finding with task evidence
metrics.source: Moderated sessions asking users to explain the result, assumptions and limitation in their own words.
metrics.cadence: Each YMYL template change and quarterly
metrics.decision: Add an explanation, worked example or caveat when a user cannot tell what the number means.

metrics.name: Verified result correctness
metrics.unit: passing test vectors and invariants
metrics.source: Independent derivations, boundary vectors and browser checks; finance and YMYL suites are the evidence.
metrics.cadence: Every push and on source-data change
metrics.decision: Any material correctness failure stops promotion regardless of traffic or conversion.

metricGroups.name: Findable — the right people can reach the right task

metrics.name: Search visibility for proven intents
metrics.unit: impressions, clicks, CTR and average position by query and URL
metrics.source: Google Search Console; segment brand, non-brand, device and page template.
metrics.decision: Select the next 10–25 pages from real queries; never derive demand from a keyword tool alone.

metrics.name: Intended index coverage
metrics.unit: intended URLs indexed and thin URLs excluded
metrics.source: Search Console indexing report plus build-sitemap.py and canonical checks.
metrics.decision: Rebuild or consolidate a page that cannot offer unique value; do not publish more thin pages.

metrics.name: Visibility in generative Search features
metrics.unit: impressions and URLs shown, where the Search Console report is available
metrics.source: Google Search Console generative AI performance report; absence of the report is recorded as unavailable.
metrics.decision: Improve the underlying useful page; do not add AI-only markup or commodity copy.

metrics.name: Earned referring domains and qualified mentions
metrics.unit: manually verified domains and mentions
metrics.source: Search Console Links plus a dated editorial log; exclude paid, exchanged, automated and self-generated links.
metrics.decision: Invest in useful tools, original findings and relationships; never buy links or chase a count.

metrics.name: Permissioned returning audience
metrics.unit: owner-approved subscribers or direct return visits
metrics.source: Provider dashboard or existing allowed analytics only, after an owner decision and privacy review.
metrics.decision: Only add a signup when the value exchange is clear, voluntary and privacy-compatible.

metrics.name: Largest Contentful Paint
metrics.unit: milliseconds at p75, mobile and desktop
metrics.source: CrUX/PageSpeed Insights field data; lab results are diagnostic, not a field pass.
metrics.decision: Protect the first screen and remove the largest blocking cost before adding visual effects.

metrics.name: Interaction to Next Paint
metrics.unit: milliseconds at p75, mobile and desktop
metrics.source: CrUX/PageSpeed Insights field data plus browser profiling of search and tool interactions.
metrics.decision: Keep task interactions responsive; the official good threshold is 200ms or less, with 150ms as an internal stretch goal.

metrics.name: Cumulative Layout Shift
metrics.unit: unitless score at p75, mobile and desktop
metrics.source: CrUX/PageSpeed Insights field data plus browser geometry checks.
metrics.decision: Reserve space for content and never trade stability for a decorative effect.

metrics.name: Critical accessibility findings
metrics.unit: count by template and severity
metrics.source: Automated checks, keyboard walkthroughs, zoom/reflow and assistive-technology spot checks.
metrics.decision: No known critical keyboard, name/role/value, contrast or reflow blocker ships.

metrics.name: Mobile task completion
metrics.unit: qualitative and quantitative session evidence by viewport
metrics.source: Real-device or device-emulation sessions at 360–390px and representative desktop widths.
metrics.decision: Mobile is a primary experience, not a final resize check.

metrics.name: Sourced high-stakes claims
metrics.unit: percent of sampled YMYL claims with a current authoritative source
metrics.source: Manual claim inventory with HMRC, NHS, legislation.gov.uk, WHO or the relevant primary source.
metrics.cadence: Each statutory or YMYL change and quarterly
metrics.decision: Unsourced or stale high-stakes claims are fixed, scoped or removed before promotion.

metrics.name: Classified network behaviour
metrics.unit: network-touching tools classified and visibly disclosed
metrics.source: scripts/check-egress.py plus manual dynamic-URL and offline checks.
metrics.decision: A new network path is classified and disclosed before it can ship.

metrics.name: Correction handling time
metrics.unit: days from verified report to visible correction
metrics.source: Public corrections log and Git history; no user identity is required.
metrics.decision: A reported material error gets an owner, source and dated resolution rather than silent editing.

metricGroups.name: Viable — revenue that does not damage the product

metrics.name: Qualified embed-licence enquiries
metrics.unit: count and source, manually verified
metrics.source: Owner inbox/bookkeeping plus allowed money-page events after the D-007 ruling; no input values.
metrics.decision: Validate the offer with real buyers before adding pages, tiers or support burden.

metrics.name: Licence contribution margin
metrics.unit: revenue minus direct fulfilment and support cost, per tier
metrics.source: Owner bookkeeping and time log; prices remain proposals until signed by the owner.
metrics.decision: Do not scale a tier that cannot pay for its maintenance and support honestly.

metrics.name: Annual licence renewal rate
metrics.unit: renewed licences divided by licences eligible to renew
metrics.source: Invoice/bookkeeping records; cohort by tier and start date.
metrics.decision: Renewal is evidence of maintained value; investigate churn before increasing acquisition effort.

metrics.name: Support hours per active licence
metrics.unit: owner support hours per licence-month
metrics.source: A simple owner time log; do not collect customer data in tools.
metrics.decision: Improve documentation or narrow the offer when support erodes contribution margin.

metrics.name: Qualified sync enquiries and closed licences
metrics.unit: count and booked value from owner records
metrics.source: Owner inbox and bookkeeping; rights and tax treatment are reviewed before a deal.
metrics.decision: Prioritise catalogue presentation and outreach that creates real conversations, never artificial plays.

metrics.name: Whole-site operating contribution
metrics.unit: collected revenue minus cash costs and valued maintainer time, GBP by month and trailing 12 months
metrics.source: Owner bookkeeping plus a simple time log; keep tools and music lines separate before showing the combined total.
metrics.decision: The site is financially viable only when the portfolio covers its real ongoing burden; a high-margin sale does not hide an unprofitable whole.

metrics.name: Revenue concentration and resilience
metrics.unit: share of trailing-12-month collected revenue by customer, channel and product line
metrics.source: Owner bookkeeping; report bands or aggregates publicly and never customer identities.
metrics.decision: Do not let one customer, platform or search channel become an unacknowledged single point of failure; diversify only after one line is proven.

experimentRules: Write the user problem, hypothesis, primary metric, guardrails, duration and stop rule before changing a live surface.
Use qualitative sessions to discover problems; do not claim a population rate from five people. Use a defensible sample and confidence interval for quantitative claims.
Change one material variable at a time when attribution matters; keep a dated control or before-state.
A win requires the primary metric to improve without a guardrail regression. If evidence is inconclusive, record inconclusive rather than shipping a victory story.
No new analytics, cookies, lead capture or customer data collection without the owner decision and privacy review already required by D-007.
Search positions, traffic, likes and catalogue count are leading or inventory measures, not substitutes for task success, correctness or contribution margin.

hardGates: Safety, material correctness, privacy, accessibility and binding owner decisions are pass/fail gates; they are never traded for reach, revenue or design points.
A candidate without dated user, search, failure, financial or statutory evidence remains discovery work and cannot outrank a measured task.
A candidate that cannot name an observable outcome, smallest reversible change and stop rule is not ready.
selectionOrder: Prevent credible harm or a materially wrong result.
Restore a broken top task or a shared path that blocks many tasks.
Remove the largest observed findability, comprehension, accessibility or performance barrier.
Run the smallest test that resolves an expensive uncertainty about usefulness, distribution or willingness to pay.
Scale a proven search, referral or commercial loop only after its guardrails and maintenance cost are known.
Add visual delight only when clarity, speed and access remain intact.
tieBreakers: Prefer stronger first-party evidence over a larger speculative reach estimate.
Prefer the higher expected user value per maintainer hour, including recurring maintenance and support rather than build effort alone.
Prefer a change that improves a reusable template or validated loop over a one-off page, unless the one-off prevents harm.
Prefer reversible work and learning value when expected outcomes are otherwise similar.
